name: No QAT (PTQ-only)
tagline: Skip fine-tuning entirely (num_steps=0); rely solely on the fixed real per-group symmetric round-to-nearest QDQ pass.
diff_from_baseline: Pure RTN PTQ control (Jacob et al. 2018, CVPR). Applies symmetric per-group round-to-nearest after no training; isolates the share of error attributable to quantization alone.

name: Straight-Through Estimator
tagline: Vanilla STE QAT: per-row, per-group symmetric fake-quant in the forward pass with identity gradient through round/clamp.
diff_from_baseline: Bengio, Léonard & Courville 2013 (arXiv:1308.3432). Baseline gradient estimator for non-differentiable quantizers; treats round as identity in the backward pass.

name: Learned Step Size Quantization
tagline: Per-group quantization scale s is a trainable parameter with the LSQ-paper gradient (g_scale = 1/sqrt(N·qmax)); STE pass-through inside the clip range.
formula: $$\hat{w} = \mathrm{round}\!\big(\mathrm{clip}(w/s, q_{\min}, q_{\max})\big)\cdot s,\;\; \frac{\partial \hat{w}}{\partial s} = \begin{cases} q_{\min}/q_{\max} & w/s\le q_{\min} \\ q_{\max}/q_{\max} & w/s\ge q_{\max} \\ \mathrm{round}(w/s) - w/s & \text{else}\end{cases}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{N\,q_{\max}}}$$
diff_from_baseline: Esser et al. 2020 (LSQ, ICLR). Learns per-channel/per-group quantization scales jointly with weights using a custom-derived gradient; widely used reference for low-bit weight QAT.

name: Finetune then PTQ (control)
tagline: Full-precision fine-tune on the calibration text under the same schedule as QAT, then apply RTN PTQ to isolate the contribution of fake-quant signal.
diff_from_baseline: Diagnostic control disentangling "better fine-tuned weights" from "genuine fake-quant signal". Same RTN PTQ as Jacob et al. 2018 but applied to fine-tuned weights.

name: AdaRound
tagline: Layer-wise adaptive rounding: learn per-weight up/down rounding decisions by minimising the squared output reconstruction error after PTQ.
diff_from_baseline: Nagel et al. 2020 (AdaRound, ICML). Optimises rounding direction per weight rather than naïve nearest-rounding, recovering substantial PTQ accuracy at low bit-widths.

name: LR-QAT
tagline: Low-rank Quantization-Aware Training: train only a low-rank update on top of a quantized backbone, drastically reducing QAT memory.
formula: $$\tilde{W} = \mathrm{Quant}(W_0) + B A,\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_o\times r},\; A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_i},\; r \ll \min(d_o,d_i)$$
diff_from_baseline: Bondarenko et al. 2024 (LR-QAT, NeurIPS / arXiv:2406.06385). Memory-efficient QAT for LLMs combining low-rank residuals with weight-quantization-aware forward.

name: PACT
tagline: Parameterised Clipping Activation: learn a per-layer clipping threshold α that bounds activations before fake-quantization (gradient via STE).
diff_from_baseline: Choi et al. 2018 (PACT, arXiv:1805.06085). Learnable activation clipping range; canonical low-bit activation-QAT method (also adapted for weight QAT).

name: Stable QAT
tagline: QAT variant focused on training stability at very low bit-widths via warm-up of fake-quant strength and gradient/scale clipping.
diff_from_baseline: Generic 'stabilised QAT' family; refers to recipes that warm up quantization strength to avoid catastrophic loss spikes at sub-4-bit precisions. Exact variant unclear without source.
